supporting_observations.claim: The account guest.rwong was created at 13:44:55 UTC by tess.hart; the creation event identifies tess.hart's logon ID as 0x5e00f30, matching her domain logon shortly beforehand.
The new account was added to the Volunteers group by tess.hart in the same logon session used to create it.

The actor, guest.<name> naming pattern, and Volunteers group addition match the documented help-desk temporary-account practice, so the available evidence supports a benign disposition for this alert.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs for 13:30–14:00 UTC were not collected due to an outage; the account creation and group-addition events are present in domain-controller security logs.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not show whether guest.rwong had any group memberships or privileges beyond the recorded Volunteers addition.
The logs do not establish whether a specific request or approval for guest.rwong existed.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: tess.hart launched MMC with DNS Manager at high integrity and the process connected to the domain controller on port 135; this is outside the alerted account-creation activity. Records T298-00001–T298-00004.

Separate review: tess.hart initiated an RDP session to FILE-ORC-01, although the supplied practice context says remote administration is performed only from WS-SBYRNE-01. This does not establish a connection to the account creation. Records T298-00026–T298-00032.

Separate review: a UserAssist registry entry references a Slack shortcut on tess.hart's workstation; Slack is not among the approved software listed in the supplied context. This does not establish a connection to the account creation. Record T298-00025.
